title: Regulatory Affairs Note — Power Supply Cost Recovery in Revalued Net Energy Metering Export Credits
content:
A revalued export rate under a retail-valued Net Energy Metering rider may include a supply-cost component drawn from the Power Supply Cost Recovery factor of the rate schedule of the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system.

**Rule.** Under the legacy rider's retail energy rate basis, the full Power Supply Cost Recovery rate of the schedule is added. Under the retail-rate-less-non-bypassable-charge basis on a residential rider, the Power Supply Cost Recovery rate multiplied by the successor supply share of 0.60, rounded to five decimals, is added. Otherwise, as for the aggregated business rider, nothing is added.

The component is added to both revalued rates, the on-peak and the off-peak alike.

## Component by rider

| Rider | Valuation basis and customer class | Supply-cost component added to each revalued rate |
|---|---|---|
| Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering | Retail energy rate; residential | The schedule's full Power Supply Cost Recovery rate |
| Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering | Retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge; residential | The Power Supply Cost Recovery rate multiplied by 0.60, rounded to five decimals |
| Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | Retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge; business | Nothing |

## Hypothetical worked figures

Hypothetical input: a hosting schedule whose Power Supply Cost Recovery factor is 0.00421 USD per kWh.

- Under Rider NEM-L the component is 0.00421.
- Under Rider NEM-R it is 0.00421 multiplied by 0.60, that is 0.002526, rounded to 0.00253.
- Under Rider NEM-A it is zero.
